$comment: E2E suite config. The harness runs every workflow graph discovered in sourceDir against the e2e-server, which fakes all providers (LLM + external/media nodes return type-correct placeholder outputs). prepareSuite.ts reads each template's embedded params; add per-id overrides below when a template needs specific inputs. ids are slugified from the filename (e.g. 'Movie Posters' -> 'movie-posters').
$excludeComment: Trigger workflows whose adapter listens forever. Their genProcess waits on a live scheduler or filesystem watcher, and the e2e-server supplies neither, so the run only ends at the timeout. That is the node behaving correctly — an interval trigger left at max_events 0 is supposed to tick forever. Webhook and manual triggers have no genProcess to loop in and stay in the suite. Delivered-event coverage for all four is packages/base-nodes/tests/trigger-examples-run.test.ts. The graph-resource templates are excluded for a different reason: each starts from a Constant.Storyboard, Constant.Timeline or Constant.Entity picker, and the e2e-server runs against an empty database, so the document a picker names does not exist and the run fails before it reaches a node. They are templates a person fills in from their own library, not self-contained graphs. Their coverage is `npm run fixtures:graph-resources`, which seeds a scratch install and runs them on the fake provider; the graph-resources harness entry runs that, and `harness gate` selects it on any diff touching them. The directed-campaign templates are excluded for a third reason: they are the five stages of one mini app (examples/apps/directed-campaign-kit.app.json), not self-contained graphs. Each consumes the artifacts the stage before it produced — the hero needs the plan directions return, the layouts need the hero image and its contract, the revision needs an accepted hero, and the reopen needs the record file the layouts wrote — so run alone on their own defaults they fail at the first validation, which is the graph behaving correctly. Directions additionally asks a model for a strict JSON contract the deterministic fake provider cannot produce. Their coverage is packages/base-nodes/tests/directed-campaign-kit.test.ts, which drives every stage's nodes through the real contracts on a provider scripted to return that JSON, and packages/app-runtime/tests/directed-campaign-kit.test.ts for the app fold.
$nativeGameComment: The native asset-pack workflow stages candidates in a project workspace. This suite runs graphs without a project, so the graph-resources fixture harness covers it with a seeded workspace.
